documents.title: Siemens Healthineers Q4 FY2026 earnings release and financial results

baseline.summary: Siemens Healthineers enters FY2027 on a solid operating footing: FY2026 revenue rose to €23,630m (+4.0% comparable) with adjusted EBIT of ~€3.8bn (16.2% margin) and free cash flow of ~€2.4bn, following a strong FY2025 (revenue €23,375m, +5.9% comparable, FCF €2,714m). Leverage is moderate and improving (net debt including pensions/EBITDA of 2.8x at FY2025-end, down from 3.3x), but the capital structure is dominated by intercompany loans and credit facilities from the Siemens Group (~€12.8bn of loans, €4.5bn of facilities) that face early-termination risk given Siemens AG's announced plan (Nov 12, 2025) to deconsolidate SHL and spin off 30% of shares. Liquidity looks adequate, with FCF and undrawn facilities covering near-term maturities and dividends more than 2x. Secular demand drivers (aging population, addressable imaging/diagnostics/radiotherapy markets of €31-37bn and €6-7bn respectively) remain intact and underpin continued mid-single-digit growth guidance for FY2027 (4.0-5.0% comparable revenue, EPS €2.20-2.40). Key open questions are peer ROTIC benchmarking (not available in these filings) and the precise impact of the Siemens deconsolidation on financing costs and segment structure (new Imaging/Precision Therapy/Diagnostics segmentation from Oct 1, 2025).

criteria.reasoning: NOPAT proxy: FY2025 EBIT €3,154m less ~22-24% tax ≈ €2,400m against average total capital employed. Total assets €44,370m (AR2025 p.140) and total equity €18,091m give TICAP in the €30-35bn range once net debt and goodwill-heavy balance sheet are netted, implying ROTIC in the low-to-mid teens, not clearly above 15% nor below 10%. Only partial multi-year data was provided (FY2019-FY2026 snapshots, not a full continuous 10y series), so confidence is low.

No peer ROTIC figures were provided in these pages, so a direct comparison cannot be made; segment adjusted EBIT margins (Imaging 23.1%, Precision Therapy 14.9%, Diagnostics 3.2% in FY2026, Q4FY2026 p.7) show internal dispersion but no external peer benchmark is available.

Addressable markets are large and growing: Imaging >€31bn, Diagnostics ~€37bn, Varian >€6bn, Advanced Therapies >€7bn in FY2025 (AR2025 p.13), driven by aging population (over-60s to more than double by 2050, AR2025 p.8) and rising non-communicable disease burden. Comparable revenue growth of 5.9% in FY2025 and 4.0% in FY2026, with FY2027 guidance of 4.0-5.0% (Q4FY2026 p.1 and p.6), confirms continued growth rather than decline.

Net debt including pensions was €12,472m against EBITDA of €4,450m, a leverage ratio of 2.8x as of Sept 30, 2025 (AR2025 p.162), down from 3.3x a year earlier - a moderate, improving level. However, most debt (€10,837m non-current + €1,919m current of ~€12,756m total loans, AR2025 p.160) is intercompany debt to the Siemens Group, which is now subject to early-termination/market-value-compensation clauses tied to the planned deconsolidation (AR2025 p.189), adding refinancing uncertainty even though absolute leverage multiples look reasonable.

FY2025 free cash flow of €2,714m (AR2025 p.22) and FY2026 of €2,446m (Q4FY2026 p.6) comfortably exceed the FY2026 maturity of €6,243m non-derivative financial liabilities spread over one year, and even cover the 5-year maturities profile (FY2026 €6,243m + FY2027 €2,098m + FY2028-30 €5,158m = ~€13.5bn, AR2025 p.177) when combined with the €2.5bn + €2.0bn Siemens AG credit facilities (AR2025 p.160) and dividends (~€1.1bn, AR2025 p.141/169). Two years of FCF (~€5.2bn) alone cover roughly 40% of the 5-year maturities, but together with undrawn facilities of ~€4bn and strong recurring cash generation, coverage exceeds 2x of annual obligations, though reliance on intercompany facilities set to change with deconsolidation is a watch item.

The analyst has tracked Siemens Healthineers across multiple annual reports from FY2019 through FY2025 and the Q4 FY2026 release, a continuous coverage history spanning more than seven years, satisfying the >1 year closely-followed threshold.
